observation.visible_scene: A wide vista of layered karst mountain silhouettes in blue-teal tones rising above a thick, undulating sea of low clouds/fog. A darker, vegetation-topped ridge protrudes from the cloud layer in the lower-right foreground. The sky is pale and hazy above the peaks.
visible_changes: The mountains and the foreground ridge remain fixed in position across all frames, indicating a static camera with no pan, tilt, or zoom.

The cloud sea below continuously churns and drifts: its surface swirls and crests slowly change shape and shift position over time, flowing around the base of the foreground ridge rather than moving as a rigid block.
Wisps of cloud near the right ridge and in the central gap between cloud masses thin, thicken, and reconfigure gradually, showing slow fluid motion of the fog layer.
A subtle overall shift in color tone/brightness occurs (early frames slightly grayer, later frames a touch more saturated cyan), but this is gradual and not tied to any object motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The wind direction or cause driving the cloud flow is not visible.
Whether the cloud layer is rising, sinking, or merely translating horizontally beyond this segment is unknown.
Conditions before the first frame and after the last frame are not shown; the motion is ongoing at both ends.
uncertain_details: The precise net drift direction of the clouds is hard to confirm from these samples; the visible change is mostly local undulation and slow redistribution.
The slight color/brightness trend could reflect real lighting change or encoding differences rather than a physical process.
No editing cut is evident; the sequence appears to be one continuous shot.
